terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to count this week's sales and find the new customers.

tasks.title: Count the scents sold
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/maps-and-sets.js`, make `countScents(sold)` return a `Map` with one entry per scent in the list: the scent is the key and how many times it appears is the value. An empty list gives an empty `Map`. The list stays as it is.

Check calls `countScents` with lists of its own, an empty one included.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on making a Map and counting with one.
Go through the list and, for each scent, set its count to what it was plus one.
Return the Map and run the file.
hints: A Map has methods of its own: `set` writes an entry, `get` reads one, `has` asks whether one is there.
The first time a scent comes up, `get` gives `undefined`, and `undefined + 1` is `NaN`. Start a new scent from 0.
Inside the loop, `counts.set(scent, (counts.get(scent) ?? 0) + 1)`, with `const counts = new Map()` before it.

tasks.title: Find the best seller
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, `bestSeller(counts)` is given a `Map` like the one `countScents` makes. Make it return the scent with the highest count. When two scents have the same highest count, the one that comes first in the Map wins. An empty Map gives `null`. The Map stays as it is.

Check calls `bestSeller` with Maps of its own, a tie and an empty Map included.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on going through a Map.
Start with no best scent yet.
Go through the entries and keep the scent whenever its count beats the best so far.
Return the best scent and run the file.
hints: for...of goes through a Map's entries, each a pair of key and value, in the order they were added.
Keep two variables, the best scent and its count. Only a count that is higher, not one that is equal, replaces them, so a tie keeps the first.
Start with `let best = null` and `let bestCount = 0`, then `for (const [scent, count] of counts)` and an `if` that asks whether this is the first or a higher count.

tasks.title: Every scent once
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `uniqueScents(sold)` return a new list with every scent in `sold` once, in the order each first appears. Use a `Set` to leave out the repeats. The list it is given stays as it is.

Check calls `uniqueScents` with lists of its own and reads your file for the Set.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on Sets.
Make a Set from the list.
Turn the Set back into a list.
Return it and run the file.
hints: A Set keeps each value once, in the order it was first added, and it can be made straight from a list.
A Set is not a list, but spread works on it: three dots inside square brackets make a list of what it holds.
The function is one line: `return [...new Set(sold)]`.

tasks.title: Who is new this week
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, first write a function of your own called `emailKey`, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It has one parameter, `email`, and returns the email with the spaces at either end taken off and every letter in lower case, so `' Noor@Mail.com'` and `'noor@mail.com'` give the same key. It only helps `newCustomers`, so it stays off the `export` line.

Then make `newCustomers(thisWeek, known)` return a list of the keys `emailKey` gives for the emails in `thisWeek` that are not the email of a known customer, each key once, in the order each first appears. Compare emails by their keys. Both lists stay as they are.

Check calls `emailKey` and `newCustomers` with emails of its own, in mixed capitals and with spaces, and reads your file for `emailKey` and the use of it inside `newCustomers`.
nextSteps: Above `newCustomers`, write `function emailKey(email) {` and its closing `}` yourself.
Make a Set of the keys of the known emails.
Go through this week's emails and keep each key that is not in that Set, once.
Return the keys as a list and run the file: only Ada is new.
hints: `trim` and `toLowerCase` from the issue on text do the work of `emailKey`.
A Set answers `has` quickly, so it is the place for the known keys. A second Set for the new keys leaves out repeats by itself.

`emailKey` is `return email.trim().toLowerCase()`. In `newCustomers`, `const knownKeys = new Set(known.map(emailKey))`, then add each key that `knownKeys.has` says no to into a second Set, and return `[...found]`.
